markdown_content: # CLAW 2026.0 Cantonese New Features Webinar — Clean Knowledge Document ## Overview of CLAW 2026.0 New/Improved Features This section introduces the webinar’s main focus: new functions and improved workflows in **CLAW 2026.0**, including avatar drawing, pattern drafting automation, string/strain visualization, lacing and gluing tools, and multiple 2D/3D/Closet/avator workflow enhancements. It also notes that the introduction timeline and supporting website resources are provided alongside the video. --- ## 3D Pencil Avatar: Draw on Avatar and Convert to Curves / 2D Paper This section explains how to use **3D Pencil Avatar** to sketch directly on an avatar, then convert the sketch into **3D curve data** or **2D paper**. ### How to enter the 3D Pencil Avatar mode 1. Create/open a new file. 2. Open an **avatar** in the file. 3. In the left **3D toolbar**, locate **3D Pen Avatar**. 4. Press and hold the icon, then choose **3D Pencil Avatar** (under the paper option). After opening the mode: - A **sketch window** appears in the upper-left of the **2D window**. - The **3D window** automatically switches to the **front** viewpoint. **Limitation:** In this mode, you **cannot rotate the eyes** (to ensure drawing accuracy). You **can zoom in/out** as needed. ### Draw and refine in the sketch window - Ensure the sketch window tool is set to **Pencil**. - Drag on the avatar surface to draw lines. - The system performs **smooth processing** to extend/beautify drawn strokes. Useful sketch options: - **Symmetric**: Draw symmetrical lines along the avatar’s middle line (useful for items like **jackets** or **skirts**). - **Conversion Guide**: Previews the draft, shows: - the draft-to-3D-pen conversion result, and - which edges are **too curved** or positioned incorrectly. - Use the guide to adjust control points. - **Viewpoint**: Use the bottom button to quickly switch between **front** and **back** viewpoints to complete outlines. ### Erase, convert, and flatten - Use the **eraser icon** in the sketch window. - Adjust eraser size. - Two round handles appear; drag them on the line segment to modify. Conversion: - Select **Convert to 3D Pen** (bottom of sketch window). - The 2D draft is projected onto the avatar surface and becomes a **3D pen curve**. - The software automatically switches to an **Edit 3D Pen Avatar** tool for immediate adjustments. If switching produces merged front-to-back continuous lines: - Select the lines and use **Flatten** to directly convert the 2D draft into **2D**. --- ## Pattern Drafter (2026.0): Auto-Convert POM/Grading, Edit Mode, and Auto-Grading This section covers **Pattern Drafter** improvements, including automatic conversion of **POM** and **Grading**, how to edit parameters safely, and how to run grading automatically. ### Auto-convert POM into Pattern Drafter 1. In the main menu, open **2D**. 2. Open **Pattern Drafter**. 3. In the **Divide** section, select an example like: - **T-shirt** - **Set In** After selecting: - A series of square data appears under the sketch window. - When converting to **GAN** (as described in the workflow), the system **automatically converts POM** based on the selected items. - In the **2D window**, the POMs update accordingly. To inspect: - Click the **POM screen** in the **Object Browser** to view submitted numbers. To modify POM: - Use **Edit POM** from the **2D toolbar**. - Click the POM in the 2D window to change values. **Update behavior:** POM numbers in both **Object Browser** and **Pattern Drafter** can update immediately. ### Warning: Editing pattern edges vs parametric values Reminder: - If you use **Edit Pattern** to directly pull paper edges, the system warns that it becomes difficult to use **Parametric Value** inside **Pattern Drafter**. - If you use **Edit in Drafter**, it returns to **Edit Mode** and continues changing numbers. - If you choose **Proceed**, the paper image is cut off from **Pattern Drafter** and becomes an ordinary paper image for manual editing. ### Edit Mode: update vs create new paper 1. Open **Pattern Drafter** via main menu. 2. Ensure the **Pattern Drafter exists in the 2D window** before the **Edit** button appears. 3. In the Pattern Drafter area, use **Create** / **Edit** buttons. In **Edit Mode**: - The paper image size is shown on the 2D paper. - Paper visuals change to a **ghost-like shape**. - Example: neck width updates. You can: - change numeric values, and - increase/decrease item size. After changes: - Two bottom-right buttons appear: - **Update**: apply directly to the original paper image. - **Create as New**: keep old paper image and create a new one. When using **Create as New**: - Multiple paper images appear in the 2D window. - **Object Browser** shows separate POM lists per paper image. - In the **upper-right dropdown** of Edit Mode: - select which paper image to edit, - unselected paper images switch to **Ghost Mode** for easier per-number handling. ### Auto-grading in Pattern Drafter 1. In upper-right, click **Add Grading**. 2. In the size table: - add desired sizes, - double-click to rename sizes. 3. Select **Base Size**, click **OK**. 4. Use **Update** after setting: - input small number on the left/right table, - input large number for the target size range. To view grading effect: - Enable **Show Grading** icon on top of the 2D window, or - check grading in **Object Browser** within the **Grading** window. If you need size changes: - return to **Edit Mode**, modify table values, then **Update**. --- ## String Map (2026.0): Fabric- and Global-Based Stretch Visualization + Strain Info This section describes improved **String Map** visualization that accounts for fabric physical properties, plus how **Fabric Mode** uses per-fabric stretch limits and how **Strain Info** provides detailed numeric inspection. ### Global Mode vs Fabric Mode **Global Mode** - Uses a fixed standard to show **absolute change** per fabric. - Visualized in **8 sections**. - Example logic: - If maximum is set to **120**, fabrics turn red depending on fabric size/standard. - A fabric like **jersey at 120% stretch** might still be comfortable, but Global Mode can still mark it red because it uses the global standard. **Fabric Mode** - Uses per-fabric **maximum value** and stretch distribution. - Divides from **100% to the fabric’s maximum** into **8 sections**. - Best for checking fit based on each fabric’s own maximum behavior. ### Stretch limit and comfort interpretation The system calculates **stretch limit** based on fabric properties. - When stretched to the maximum value, you may feel uncomfortable. Examples given: - Knit jersey stretch limit differs across fabric types. - The simulation uses updated fabric width and properties, so results can differ from Global Mode. **Important workflow caveat:** If you change fabric or its physical properties, remember to press **Refresh** (or use the top button to update all fabric data).
